en.title: 10.26–11.1 | This Week's Best AI Papers

en.title: AI+FDE: A qualified FDE has to work the business hands-on alongside veteran operators, then turn those experience-based solutions into Skills | Lu Yufeng, co-founder and COO of Shenkong Zhixu, shares
en.summary:
Word count: 5,139
Reading time: about 17 minutes

FDE (Field Delivery Engineer) is a pivotal role in getting AI into production, requiring deep presence on the business front line to grasp tacit knowledge and real-world constraints. Shenkong Zhixu validated this through two cases — embroidery and customs declaration: FDE-driven process modeling and OCR optimization markedly improved delivery turnaround and cost efficiency. The essence is converting experiential judgment into data and rules that can be engineered.

- FDEs must personally execute the business process, not just observe and take notes;
- The embroidery project pivoted to end-to-end generation from original artwork to stitch path, sidestepping the bottleneck of imitating operator behavior;
- Customs declaration OCR, iterated on site, cut document processing time by 97% and cost by 86%.

Intended for AI delivery engineers, vertical-domain Agent product managers, and industrial AI solution architects.

At the main forum of 1024 ModelPower Factory · AI Community Day, Shenkong Zhixu co-founder and COO Lu Yufeng delivered a keynote titled "FDE: The Core Competitiveness of AI Deployment."

Notably, Shenkong Zhixu is an AI company co-founded by Lu Yufeng and former DingTalk CEO Ye Jun, focused on Agent Nine, an AI business agent for cross-border e-commerce scenarios.

en.title: Sharing an AI development workflow I've been really happy with lately — it mainly requires two apps, Magpie and Codex App. Magpie is absolutely fantastic: since switching over from cc, all my skills, MCP and providers are now connected to my Agents through Magpie.
en.summary:
Sharing an AI development workflow that's been working really smoothly for me lately. It mainly requires two apps: Magpie and Codex App.

Magpie is genuinely fantastic. Since switching over from cc, I've connected all my skills, MCP, and providers to my Agents through Magpie.
And the local reverse proxy also provides a lot of quota for other models, but I still chose to use it alongside CPA — I'll explain why later.

First up is Magpie's routing feature. I have different models split up the work directly, then in Agents.md I assign the sub-agent to this smart router. This avoids burning too much quota on very basic tasks, or having unused free quota from various providers pile up (once connected, consumption is still pretty fast — I haven't opened many new accounts, and basically each free grant doesn't last more than two or three days).

Next…
en.reason: A workflow built on Magpie and Codex App routes all skills, MCP servers and providers through Magpie into Agents, with a sub-agent set in Agents.md as a smart router so different models divide tasks and basic work stops burning scarce quota.

I started using GrokBot in August. To be honest, I spotted a glitch deal on SuperGrok Heavy late one night and bought it on impulse. The purchase came with a Cursor membership, a SuperGrok Heavy membership, and a GrokBot membership, which X was pushing hard at the time.

en.summary:
Word count: 5,139
Reading time: about 17 minutes

FDE (Field Delivery Engineer) is a pivotal role in getting AI into production, requiring deep presence on the business front line to grasp tacit knowledge and real-world constraints. Shenkong Zhixu validated this through two cases — embroidery and customs declaration: FDE-driven process modeling and OCR optimization markedly improved delivery turnaround and cost efficiency. The essence is converting experiential judgment into data and rules that can be engineered.

- FDEs must personally execute the business process, not just observe and take notes;
- The embroidery project pivoted to end-to-end generation from original artwork to stitch path, sidestepping the bottleneck of imitating operator behavior;
- Customs declaration OCR, iterated on site, cut document processing time by 97% and cost by 86%.

en.summary:
Sharing an AI development workflow that's been working really smoothly for me lately. It mainly requires two apps: Magpie and Codex App.

Magpie is genuinely fantastic. Since switching over from cc, I've connected all my skills, MCP, and providers to my Agents through Magpie.
And the local reverse proxy also provides a lot of quota for other models, but I still chose to use it alongside CPA — I'll explain why later.

First up is Magpie's routing feature. I have different models split up the work directly, then in Agents.md I assign the sub-agent to this smart router. This avoids burning too much quota on very basic tasks, or having unused free quota from various providers pile up (once connected, consumption is still pretty fast — I haven't opened many new accounts, and basically each free grant doesn't last more than two or three days).

Next…
